ai.text:
This bill moves certain education and job-training responsibilities from the Department of Education to the Department of Labor's Employment and Training Administration. The main responsibilities being moved are those of the Department of Education's Office of Career, Technical, and Adult Education, which runs adult education and family literacy programs under Title II of the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act, as well as career and technical education programs under the Carl D. Perkins Career and Technical Education Act of 2006.

The bill also moves all staff and funding connected to these transferred responsibilities to the Labor Department's Employment and Training Administration. It notes that on July 15, 2025, the Department of Education announced an agreement under which the Labor Department would manage competitions, provide technical help, and combine these education programs with its existing programs. Under that arrangement, the Department of Education must still keep its legal responsibilities and oversight of the programs.

The bill assigns the Office of Management and Budget a role in the transfer. That office must make sure the change does not create a net increase in full-time employees at either the Employment and Training Administration or the Department of Education. It must also certify to specified congressional committees that the bill is being followed.

Finally, the transfer does not affect any lawsuits, proceedings, or applications for benefits, services, licenses, permits, certificates, or financial assistance that are already pending when the bill becomes law.

summary.text:
Less Bureaucracy, Better Workforce Development Act
This bill transfers specified functions relating to education and workforce development programs from the Department of Education (ED) to the Department of Labor's Employment and Training Administration (ETA).
Specifically, the bill transfers to the ETA all the functions and authorities exercised by ED before the bill's effective date related to ED's Office of Career, Technical, and Adult Education. This office administers adult education and family literacy programs under Title II of the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act and career and technical education programs under the Carl D. Perkins Career and Technical Education Act of 2006. (On July 15, 2025, ED announced an interagency agreement with Labor for Labor to manage competitions, provide technical assistance, and integrate ED's programs with Labor's existing programs, while ED must maintain its statutory responsibilities and program oversight.)
Additionally, the bill transfers to the ETA all personnel and appropriations related to the functions that are transferred under this bill.
The bill outlines the authority of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) related to the functions that are transferred under this bill, including that OMB must ensure that this bill does not create a net increase in full-time equivalent employees at the ETA or ED. Further, OMB must certify compliance with the bill to specified congressional committees.
The transfer of these functions does not affect any suits, proceedings, or applications for benefits, services, licenses, permits, certificates, or financial assistance that are pending on the date of this bill's enactment.
